newsitem.title: USA: U.S. May spot natgas climbs 25-30 cts over April 1.
newsitem.headline: U.S. May spot natgas climbs 25-30 cts over April 1.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices for May 1 delivery edged higher Friday, led by an uptick in incremental demand and the anticipation of warmer weather and heftier storage injections next month, industry sources said.
Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub for May 1 rose two to three cents to $2.14-2.18 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), indicating a gain of about 30 cents from April indices.
Meanwhile, weekend prices at the hub firmed more than five cents to about $2.20 as cooler-than-normal weather covered northern Texas.
Similarly in south Texas, May prices carried about a 30-cent premium over April 1 to about $2.05. For weekend deliveries, prices rose by about five cents to $2.06-2.12.
In the Northeast, May New York city-gate prices were talked at $2.40-2.45, up about 20 cents from April indices. Weekend prices were also slightly stronger around $2.45.
Appalachian prices for next month were quoted at $2.34-2.38 on Columbia and $2.35-2.39 on CNG.
At the Chicago city-gate, May gas traded at $2.21 and $2.22, while weekend prices hovered around $2.20. Detroit for next month was talked in the low-$2.30s.
Elsewhere in the Midcontinent, May prices rose a couple of cents to about $2 early and the mid-$1.90s in late morning trade, up more than 25 cents from April 1.
Demarcation was quoted mostly in the high-$1.90s.
Weekend prices in the Midcontinent were for the most part in convergence with May in the mid-to-high $1.90s.
Further west, Permian basin prices for May 1 remained about 30 cents over April indices in the low-$1.90s, while weekend prices were stuck in the high-$1.80s to low-$1.90s.
At the southern California border, May prices were talked at $2.00-2.05, up about 25-30 cents from April 1.
